title: Cancel the registration on a written-off vehicle
summary: Learn how to complete the cancellation of a vehicle registration after a vehicle has been written off.
intro:
If your vehicle is classified as written-off by the insurer, it will be recorded on the NSW Written-Off Vehicle Register.

You'll be notified in writing that the vehicle has been written-off and the registration cancelled.

You then need to take the number plates to a Service NSW Centre within 14 days to complete the cancellation.
who_can_apply: The vehicle must be classified as written-off by the insurer.
what_you_need: The PDF form: Number Plates and/or Cancellation of Registration Application
Your current Certificate of Registration (if available)
The number plates (or a written declaration that the plates were lost or stolen, a police event number, or a receipt if surrendered interstate)
A police incident report or insurance statement showing the date of the incident (if applicable)
For refunds: A police incident report or insurance statement showing the date of the incident

how_to_steps.text: Gather the required documents and the number plates (if available) and visit a service centre to complete the cancellation.

faqs.q: What happens when my vehicle is written off?
faqs.a: If your vehicle is classified as written-off by the insurer, it will be recorded on the NSW Written-Off Vehicle Register, and you will be notified in writing that the registration has been cancelled.

faqs.q: How do I complete the cancellation of my registration?
faqs.a: You must take the number plates to a Service NSW Centre within 14 days to complete the cancellation.

faqs.q: Am I eligible for a refund?
faqs.a: You may be eligible for a refund of the unused portion of the motor vehicle tax and any remaining CTP insurance. For more information on refunds, visit the State Insurance Regulatory Authority website.
